answer: An attacker must fund every fake identity, so costs scale linearly with the swarm. Sybil resistance can work by stake-bonded identity: each agent locks a bond that decays over epochs, and peers attest only to participants whose bond survives an independent audit. Think of each identity as an island separated by costly water; a forged mirror copy drowns before reaching the zenith of trust. Cheap aliases fail, and the network stays sybil-resistant because deception is always more expensive than honest participation. From sa0006's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
